claims.text: Intake (psychiatric hospital admission) — Legal status: part of the patient's identification data.
claims.quote: (1) The identification data must include the patient's legal status.

claims.text: Intake (psychiatric hospital admission) — Admitting diagnosis: a provisional or admitting diagnosis at admission, including intercurrent (medical) diseases as well as psychiatric diagnoses.
claims.quote: (2) A provisional or admitting diagnosis must be made on every patient at the time of admission, and must include the diagnoses of intercurrent diseases as well as the psychiatric diagnoses.

claims.text: Intake (psychiatric hospital admission) — Reasons for admission: clearly documented as stated by the patient and/or others significantly involved.
claims.quote: (3) The reasons for admission must be clearly documented as stated by the patient and/or others significantly involved.

claims.text: Intake (psychiatric hospital admission) — Social history: social service records (interviews with the patient, family and others) assess home plans, family attitudes and community resource contacts, and include a social history.
claims.quote: (4) The social service records, including reports of interviews with patients, family members, and others, must provide an assessment of home plans and family attitudes, and community resource contacts as well as a social history.

claims.text: Intake (psychiatric hospital admission) — Neuro exam: when indicated, a complete neurological exam is recorded with the admission physical.
claims.quote: (5) When indicated, a complete neurological examination must be recorded at the time of the admission physical examination.

claims.text: Intake (psychiatric hospital admission) — Psychiatric evaluation: completed within 60 hours of admission, with a medical history, mental status, onset of illness and circumstances leading to admission, attitudes and behavior, estimates of intellectual functioning, memory and orientation, and an inventory of the patient's assets written descriptively, not interpretively.
claims.quote: (b) Standard: Psychiatric evaluation. Each patient must receive a psychiatric evaluation that must— (1) Be completed within 60 hours of admission; (2) Include a medical history; (3) Contain a record of mental status; (4) Note the onset of illness and the circumstances leading to admission; (5) Describe attitudes and behavior; (6) Estimate intellectual functioning, memory functioning, and orientation; and (7) Include an inventory of the patient's assets in descriptive, not interpretative, fashion.

claims.text: Progress (treatment plan and progress notes) — Treatment plan: an individual comprehensive plan based on the patient's strengths and disabilities, with a substantiated diagnosis, short-term and long-range goals, the specific treatment modalities, each team member's responsibilities, and documentation that justifies the diagnosis and treatment.
claims.quote: (1) Each patient must have an individual comprehensive treatment plan that must be based on an inventory of the patient's strengths and disabilities. The written plan must include— (i) A substantiated diagnosis; (ii) Short-term and long-range goals; (iii) The specific treatment modalities utilized; (iv) The responsibilities of each member of the treatment team; and (v) Adequate documentation to justify the diagnosis and the treatment and rehabilitation activities carried out.

claims.text: Progress (treatment plan and progress notes) — Progress notes: at least weekly for the first 2 months and at least monthly after that, with recommendations for treatment-plan revisions and a precise assessment of progress against the plan.
claims.quote: The frequency of progress notes is determined by the condition of the patient but must be recorded at least weekly for the first 2 months and at least once a month thereafter and must contain recommendations for revisions in the treatment plan as indicated, as well as precise assessment of the patient's progress in accordance with the original or revised treatment plan.

claims.text: Consult — Billing a consult (Medicare): Medicare doesn't pay the CPT consultation codes (inpatient 99252-99255, office/outpatient 99242-99245); report the correct E/M visit code for the consult instead.
claims.quote: Medicare doesn't recognize these CPT codes for Part B payment purposes: Inpatient consultation codes, CPT codes 99252-99255 O/O consultation codes, CPT codes 99242-99245 Medicare recognizes these telehealth consultation codes for payment: HCPCS codes G0406-G0408 HCPCS codes G0425-G0427 If you provide services using CPT consultation codes, you should report the correct E/M visit code to bill for these services.

claims.text: D/C (discharge summary) — Discharge summary: a recap of the hospitalization, recommendations from appropriate services on follow-up or aftercare, and a brief summary of the patient's condition at discharge.
claims.quote: The record of each patient who has been discharged must have a discharge summary that includes a recapitulation of the patient's hospitalization and recommendations from appropriate services concerning follow-up or aftercare as well as a brief summary of the patient's condition on discharge.
